title: Light Vintage Dutch Cream Bisque
description: Malty, light, and nostalgic, this creamy bisque features the subtle flavors of dry sherry.
instructions: In a medium saucepan, melt the butter over medium heat. Add the chopped onion and cook until softened, about 5 minutes.
Add the minced garlic and cook for 1 minute, until fragrant.
Add the flour and cook for 1 minute, stirring constantly.
Gradually add the dry sherry, whisking constantly to avoid lumps.
Bring the mixture to a simmer and cook for 2 minutes.
Add the heavy cream and bring the mixture to a simmer.
Reduce the heat to low and let simmer for 5 minutes, or until the soup has thickened slightly.
Stir in the grated Gruyère cheese, nutmeg, salt, and black pepper until melted and smooth.
Stir in the malted milk powder and sugar until dissolved.
Bring the mixture to a simmer and cook for an additional 2 minutes.
Remove the saucepan from the heat and let cool slightly.
Strain the mixture through a fine-mesh sieve into a blender or food processor.
Add the water for spherification and blend until smooth.
Spherify the bisque using a spherification agent, such as sodium alginate or calcium chloride.
Serve the bisque chilled, garnished with a sprinkle of malted milk powder, if desired.
Chill the bisque in the refrigerator for at least 2 hours before serving.
If desired, garnish with a sprinkle of paprika or chopped fresh herbs, such as chives or parsley.
Serve the bisque in demitasse cups or small glasses, if desired.
If not serving immediately, store the bisque in an airtight container in the refrigerator for up to 3 days.
To reheat the bisque, stir in a little cream or milk and reheat over low heat, whisking constantly, until warm and smooth.
Serve the bisque hot, garnished with a sprinkle of paprika or chopped fresh herbs, if desired.
